evidence.text: Stoa develops an AI-powered platform that brings together drawings, schedules, and quality and safety reports to help construction teams manage project information, monitor progress, and coordinate operations across complex building sites.

Stoa | AI for construction projects, answered from your own documents Home Product Case examples About us FI Log in Book a demo FI Book a demo News €3.5M pre-seed led by Lifeline Ventures Build on what your construction project already knows. Stoa reads the drawings, specifications, contracts, schedule and site records your project already holds, and answers from them, with the document and page behind every sentence. What Stoa does on a project Connects to your systems, answers from them, tracks what changes, and turns what it finds into work. Connects to the systems you already run Read-only sync from M-Files, SharePoint, Dalux, Congrid and the rest, keeping the permissions each one already set. The product in detail → Linked information → Answers questions, with the page behind each one Ask in plain language and get an answer from the drawings, specifications, contracts, schedule, quality inspections and meeting minutes, each sentence cited to its source. Open a drawing, click a wall type or door tag, and the detail or clause that governs it opens beside the plan. Ask your project → Turns findings into reports, tasks and skills An RFI, a failed inspection or a slipped delivery arrives with its drawings, clause and the activity it blocks. Export it as a report, assign it as a task, or save the way you handled it as a skill. A document bank and a schedule sit underneath, each usable on its own. From information to output → Skills → Knows what has changed on site Reissued drawings, revised specifications and moved dates arrive in one feed, filtered to your scope. Two revisions side by side show what the designer moved. The overview shows where the project stands. Integrations Stoa connects the systems you already use on site and brings all of the project's information into one place: drawings, specifications, contracts, RFIs, the programme and inspections. Read-only, and it stays in sync. And more on request. Read-only, with your existing permissions. New integrations added every week 01 Linked information 02 Ask your project 03 From information to output 04 Skills 05 Change tracking 06 Situational awareness 07 Findings & automations Linked information Stoa maps how everything on the project links together, so its answers draw on the whole picture and you can click from one document to the next. Every code on the sheet is live Wall types, finish codes, door tags and drawing numbers in callouts can all be clicked on the sheet. Click a code to see everywhere it appears Click a wall type to open the detail that defines it, the schedule that lists it and the specification clause that governs it. The reference, open at the right place Each result opens the document at the exact location, so you do not have to search through it. Find Find answers faster. Ask your project Ask anything and see where the answer came from. You find information far faster, and can see what was decided, and when, at any point in the project. One question, every document that bears on it Covers drawings, specifications, contracts, minutes, the schedule, inspections from your quality app, and email. It reads the drawings themselves, not only the text around them. Citations you can check Every sentence links to the document and page it came from, so you can check it before you pass it on. Works across languages Ask in your own language, even if the documents are written in another. Point it at a document with @ Steer a question to a document or folder, at a desk or out on site from your phone. Operate Get the work done faster. From information to output Plans, claims and reviews that took days are drafted from the project's own documents, and they include everything that should be in them. A work-phase plan, drafted from its drawings Choose the phase and its documents. Stoa checks the inputs, flags what is missing and drafts the plan: methods, resources, schedule, quality and safety. Claims Drafted from the evidence and costs in the record, ready to send. Contract review Risks, responsibilities, costs and schedule, each cited to its clause. Tender requests Scope, attachments, recipients and the email, put together from the package. Skills Do something once with Stoa, save it, and it is done the same way next time. Nobody starts from zero, and a good way of working spreads across the project. Saved once, used by anyone on the project A skill is picked from the composer like a tool, and runs the same steps on whatever you point it at. Use Stoa's, or write your own A saved way of working: draft a claim from the record, prepare a meeting from the open actions, check a contract for risk, write an ITP on your own template. Use Stoa's, or write your own and share it with the project. Pinned where you work Your most used skills sit at the top of the composer's menu. Monitor Never miss what changes. Change tracking Stoa knows what has changed and what it touches. Compare versions side by side and follow every update in the change feed, so you pass on what matters and miss less. All project changes in one place Stoa finds changes by comparing revisions, whether or not anyone announced them. Each morning a summary of yesterday's changes goes out by email. Filtered to your discipline You see the changes that touch the work you are responsible for. Which document, which revision, what depends on it Each change shows which document it is, which revision it supersedes, what depends on it, and where it now conflicts with another discipline. Side-by-side revisions Compare two revisions of a drawing next to each other. Drawing comparison See what actually moved on the sheet, such as a dimension, a wall type or a whole region, rather than relying on the revision note. Situational awareness The overview shows the whole project on one page, so everyone knows what is happening and decides better. The project on one page What is stuck, and what it stops Stoa finds what is holding work up, such as a drawing an activity is waiting on, an approval that never came back, or a revision that moved a date. This week's changes and open RFIs The documents reissued this week, the RFIs still open, and the decisions taken, beside the programme. The programme, with what each activity depends on It works because the programme is linked to the documents it depends on, and those documents to what changed. Findings & automations Stoa follows the checks that should happen, so you don't have to, and brings up new things you would otherwise miss. Checks that run when you want them to An automation runs a prompt on a schedule and posts its report to the project, so the check happens before anyone asks. Reports Export the result as a report in Word, Excel or PDF. How Stoa reads a construction project Cited to the page Every answer points to where it came from: the page of a drawing, the row of a programme, the entry in a quality app. When the documents do not hold the answer, Stoa says so.
